"2D A Tetris game. Where it's kind of RPG style. Where every 2 lines you complete sends an extra line to your opponent below. And 3 lines sends 2 lines to your opponent. Doing Tetris making 4 lines will sends 4 lines to the oponent. T-spin single It would send 2 lines to the opponent. A double T-spin would send 4 lines, and a triple T-spin would send 6 lines to the opponent. And it possesses magic that can help or hinder the opponent. Like clearing a line, another, and leaving every piece being played further to the right or left, which can leave no gaps.Use a barrier that protects against attacks or magic from an opponent for a period of time. And several others.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D RPG-style Tetris duel with attack lines and magic spells.

## Requirements
- Clear 2 lines to send 1 line; 3 lines to send 2; 4 lines to send 4.
- T-spin single sends 2 lines, double sends 4, and triple sends 6.
- Include spells that help or hinder the opponent, such as skewing their pieces, plus a temporary defensive barrier.
- Build directly without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained browser game named RuneStack with a simulated AI opponent.
- Added three spells: Emberfall burns an enemy row, Aegis Veil blocks attacks for 8 seconds, and Widdershins skews three enemy spawns.
- Added combo bonuses, mana earned from line clears, responsive touch controls, and keyboard controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game UI and gameplay in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added attacks, T-spin attack scoring, garbage rows, opponent AI, spells, pause/restart, score, timer, and combat log.
- Checked JavaScript syntax with `node --check game.js`.
- Ran the game in Playwright, tested starting, moving, dropping a piece, and casting Widdershins.
- Captured desktop and mobile screenshots.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally test line-clear and T-spin attack mappings and inspect the latest UI after the favicon change.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup and controls.
- `styles.css`: Desktop and mobile presentation.
- `game.js`: Game engine, opponent, attacks, spells, and input handling.
- `screenshots/rune-stack.jpg`: Desktop screenshot.
- `screenshots/rune-stack-mobile.jpg`: Mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright smoke test showed score incremented to `000030` after a move and hard drop; Widdershins reduced mana from 3 to 0 and showed `HEXED ×3`.
- Spell costs are 2 mana for Emberfall and Aegis Veil, 3 for Widdershins.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D RPG-style Tetris duel with attack lines and magic spells.
- Expand RuneStack with slower falling pieces, a 400-enemy roster, 20 additional spells, and player health and mana.

## Requirements
- Send 1 line for clearing 2 lines, 2 for clearing 3, and 4 for clearing 4; T-spin single/double/triple send 2/4/6 lines.
- Include helpful and hindering spells, including a temporary defensive barrier; mana is consumed when casting spells.
- The enemy should move and drop pieces, with varied difficulty and some enemies having magic while others do not.
- Add a player health bar and 20 new types of magic.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained browser game with an AI opponent.
- The existing game has Emberfall, Aegis Veil, and Widdershins, plus combo bonuses, mana from line clears, touch and keyboard controls, pause/restart, score, timer, and combat log.
- The expanded roster is being represented as 400 generated enemy entries across 20 species and 20 epithets, with tier-scaled stats and some non-magical enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the original RuneStack game in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `game.js`; prior smoke tests covered starting, moving, dropping a piece, and casting Widdershins.
- Added player health-bar markup and replaced the fixed three-spell list with a generated-list container.
- Added 23 spell definitions (the original three plus 20 additional spells), 400 generated enemy definitions, and player/enemy combat-related state fields in `game.js`.

### Active
- Integrate the generated spells and enemy roster into game startup, combat, and UI.
- Implement enemy-specific movement/drop/attack/magic behavior, slower player gravity, player health damage and healing, and spell mana costs/effects.
- Check syntax, run browser tests, and review the UI after the changes.

### Blocked
- `game.js` has not been syntax-checked since the latest edits; the new `readEnemyIndex()` expression appears to be missing a closing parenthesis and likely needs correction.

## Next Move
1. Fix and syntax-check `game.js`.
2. Connect the spell definitions and 400-enemy roster to rendered controls and gameplay, including health, mana, enemy difficulty, and magic behavior.
3. Test gameplay and responsive layout in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup, player health bar, and generated spell-list container.
- `game.js`: Game engine and latest unfinished spell, enemy, and state additions.
- `styles.css`: Health-bar, spell-list, and responsive styling.
- `screenshots/rune-stack.jpg`: Existing desktop screenshot.
- `screenshots/rune-stack-mobile.jpg`: Existing mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The 23 spell definitions and 400 enemy records are currently data/state additions; gameplay and UI integration remain unfinished.

## Objective
- Complete RuneStack as a playable 2D RPG-style Tetris duel against an AI opponent, with attacks, spells, health, and mana.
- Expand gameplay with slower falling pieces, enemy variety and difficulty, and 20 additional spells.

## Requirements
- Attack lines: 1 for clearing 2 lines, 2 for 3 lines, and 4 for 4 lines; T-spin single/double/triple send 2/4/6 lines.
- Include helpful and hindering spells, including a temporary defensive barrier; casting consumes mana.
- Enemies move and drop pieces, with varied difficulty and some magical and some non-magical.
- Add a player health bar and 20 additional types of magic.
- Include soft and hard drops for both player and enemy pieces.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained browser game with an AI opponent.
- The roster is represented by 400 generated enemies from 20 species and 20 epithets, with tier-scaled stats and some non-magical enemies.
- The spell definitions include the original three spells plus 20 additions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing game implementation includes Tetris boards, attacks, line clears, T-spins, combos, mana from line clears, keyboard/touch controls, pause/restart, score, timer, and combat log.
- Added player health-bar markup and generated spell-list container in `index.html`; added styling for health and spell-list layouts in `styles.css`.
- Added 23 spell definitions, 400 generated enemy definitions, expanded combat state, player damage/healing helpers, and a multi-effect `castSpell` implementation in `game.js`.
- Corrected the missing closing parenthesis in `readEnemyIndex()`.

### Active
- Finish connecting generated spells and enemy roster to startup, rendered UI, and combat.
- Integrate enemy-specific movement/drop/attack/magic timing, player gravity, health, and spell effects consistently.
- Syntax-check and test gameplay and responsive layout in a browser.

### Blocked
- `game.js` has not been syntax-checked or browser-tested since recent edits.

## Next Move
1. Run a syntax check on `game.js` and resolve any parse/runtime errors.
2. Connect `renderSpellbook()` to startup and adapt UI event/key bindings to the generated spells and their costs.
3. Integrate foe-specific stats and behavior into `enemyThink()`, `updateEnemy()`, and the attack loop; verify health, mana, and spells work end to end.
4. Test gameplay and responsive layout in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, generated spells/enemies, and unfinished integrations.
- `index.html`: Game UI, health-bar markup, and spell-list container.
- `styles.css`: Health bar and spell-list styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `renderSpellbook()` exists but is not called, so `#spellList` remains empty; the existing spell-button listener also runs against an empty list.

- `updateUI()` now expects `#playerHp`, `#playerHpText`, `#enemyHp`, and `#enemyHpText` markup.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete RuneStack as a playable 2D RPG-style Tetris duel against an AI opponent, with attacks, spells, health, and mana.
- Expand gameplay with slower falling pieces, varied enemies, and 20 additional spells.

## Requirements
- Attacks: clear 2/3/4 lines to send 1/2/4 lines; T-spin single/double/triple sends 2/4/6 lines.
- Include helpful and hindering spells, including a temporary defensive barrier; casting consumes mana.
- Include varied enemies, some magical and some non-magical, with different difficulty and piece behavior.
- Add a player health bar and 20 additional spell types.
- Support soft and hard drops for player and enemy pieces.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained browser game with an AI opponent.
- The enemy roster has 400 generated enemies from 20 species and 20 epithets, with tier-scaled stats.
- The spell definitions include the original three spells plus 20 additions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing game includes Tetris boards, line attacks, T-spins, combos, mana, keyboard/touch controls, pause/restart, score, timer, and combat log.
- Added player/enemy health UI and spell-list markup in `index.html`; health and spell-list styling in `styles.css`.
- Added 23 spell definitions, generated enemy definitions, expanded combat state, health helpers, and spell-effect handling in `game.js`.
- Added foe-specific AI timing, hard-drop probability, attack intervals, magic/silence behavior, attack damage, and gravity adjustments.
- Connected enemy identity and tier display to reset/start; victory advances and persists the roster index.
- Fixed a malformed token introduced during enemy-spawn editing.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest enemy behavior and combat edits.

### Active
- Finish spellbook/UI integration: call `renderSpellbook()` and update keyboard spell bindings for the full spell list.
- Verify enemy/player drop, health, attack, and spell effects; address edge cases such as non-magical enemies and ineffective spells consuming mana.
- Run syntax checks and browser gameplay/responsive-layout tests after the latest edits.

### Blocked
- `game.js` has not been syntax-checked or browser-tested since the latest edits.

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and resolve any parse/runtime errors.
2. Call `renderSpellbook()` during initialization and update key bindings and UI event handlers for generated spells.
3. Review combat edge cases, including garbage delivery, shield/mirror interactions, non-magical enemy behavior, and mana use when effects cannot apply.
4. Test gameplay and responsive layout in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, spellbook, enemy roster, AI, combat, and unfinished UI integration.
- `index.html`: Game UI, health bars, and spell-list container.
- `styles.css`: Health-bar and spell-list styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `renderSpellbook()` exists but is not called, leaving `#spellList` empty; initialization still attaches listeners only to currently rendered `.spell-card` elements.
- Keyboard controls still map only `1`, `2`, and `3` to the original spells.
- The last edits changed enemy attack timing and `hurtPlayer()`/`enemyClear()` behavior; these changes still need validation.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish RuneStack as a playable 2D RPG-style Tetris duel against an AI opponent, with attacks, spells, health, and mana.
- Complete and validate the expanded enemy roster, slower falling pieces, and 20 additional spells.

## Requirements
- Clearing 2/3/4 lines sends 1/2/4 attack lines; T-spin single/double/triple sends 2/4/6 lines.
- Include helpful and hindering spells, including a temporary defensive barrier; casting consumes mana.
- Include varied magical and non-magical enemies with different difficulty and piece behavior.
- Add a player health bar and 20 additional spell types.
- Support soft and hard drops for player and enemy pieces.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained browser game with an AI opponent.
- The enemy roster has 400 generated enemies from 20 species and 20 epithets, with tier-scaled stats.
- The spell definitions include the original three spells plus 20 additions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented spellbook rendering, click-to-cast buttons, and keyboard casting for spells 1–10.
- Added spell precondition checks for full health, absent incoming lines, non-magical foes, and an already-pending Thorn Pact.
- Updated attack handling so blocked or fatal enemy attacks do not add garbage; corrected the hard-drop label in `index.html`.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest combat edits; Playwright Chromium was installed after the first browser launch failed.

### Active
- Validate the latest changes with syntax and diff checks, then launch the game in a browser and inspect gameplay and responsive layout.
- Review remaining combat and spell interactions, including spell effects, garbage delivery, and mana use.

### Blocked
- Browser testing has not yet been rerun after installing Chromium.

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Retry `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`; check console output and verify the spellbook, start flow, boards, controls, combat, and mobile layout.
3. Fix any issues discovered and summarize validation results; changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, spellbook, enemy roster, AI, combat, and keyboard controls.
- `index.html`: Game UI, health bars, spell-list container, and board controls.
- `styles.css`: Health-bar, spell-list, and responsive styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started in tmux on port 3002.
- The first browser launch failed with `Browser "chromium" is not installed`; `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` then completed successfully.
- Enemy attacks now only add garbage if `hurtPlayer()` did not block the attack and the duel is still running.

## Objective
- Finish RuneStack as a playable 2D RPG-style Tetris duel against an AI, with attacks, spells, health, and mana.
- Validate the expanded enemy roster, slower falling pieces, and 20 additional spells.

## Requirements
- Clearing 2/3/4 lines sends 1/2/4 attack lines; T-spin single/double/triple sends 2/4/6 lines.
- Include helpful and hindering spells, including a temporary defensive barrier; casting consumes mana.
- Include varied magical and non-magical enemies with different difficulty and piece behavior.
- Add a player health bar and 20 additional spell types.
- Support soft and hard drops for player and enemy pieces.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained browser game with an AI opponent.
- The enemy roster has 400 generated enemies from 20 species and 20 epithets, with tier-scaled stats.
- The spell definitions include the original three spells plus 20 additions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented spellbook rendering, click-to-cast buttons, and keyboard casting for spells 1–10.
- Added spell precondition checks for full health, absent incoming lines, non-magical foes, and an already-pending Thorn Pact.
- Updated attack handling so blocked or fatal enemy attacks do not add garbage; corrected the hard-drop label in `index.html`.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Launched the game in Chromium; confirmed 23 spell buttons, duel start, spell casting consuming mana, and touch hard-drop input affecting the score.
- Checked the mobile layout at 390×844: touch controls are visible, game board is present, and no horizontal document overflow was reported; no console errors were reported.

### Active
- Finish browser validation of gameplay, combat and spell effects, and responsive layout; fix any issues found.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the mobile and desktop screenshots and verify gameplay controls, attacks, garbage delivery, and representative spell effects.
2. Run final syntax and diff checks; summarize the results and note that changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, spellbook, enemy roster, AI, combat, and keyboard/touch controls.
- `index.html`: Game UI, health bars, spell list, and board controls.
- `styles.css`: Health-bar, spell-list, and responsive styling.

- Changes are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve RuneStack so the player receives incoming lines only when the opponent clears at least two lines, and make the enemy AI plan piece placements to complete lines while showing the correct next piece.

## Requirements
- Timed enemy attacks should not add incoming lines to the player; incoming lines should result from enemy line clears of two or more.
- Enemy AI should choose placements that work toward completing lines and display its actual next piece.

## Decisions
- Replace the enemy’s random placement selection with a board-evaluating placement search that rewards line clears and penalizes stack height, holes, and uneven surfaces.
- Give the enemy a separate piece bag so its next-piece preview can match its spawn sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added separate enemy piece-bag generation with `nextEnemyType()`.
- Replaced random enemy placement choices with a placement scorer and target rotation/column planning.

### Active
- Finish wiring enemy piece previews and reset behavior to the separate enemy bag; verify the preview matches the next spawned piece.
- Remove timed-attack garbage and verify incoming player garbage comes only from enemy clears of two or more lines.
- Test enemy planning, combat behavior, and regressions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update enemy preview initialization and bag reset in `game.js`; ensure `nextTypePreview` is seeded from the enemy bag and used consistently.
2. Change timed enemy attacks so they do not add garbage lines; preserve the requirement that enemy clears of two or more lines can damage/send garbage.
3. Run syntax checks and browser tests for AI line completion, preview accuracy, and incoming-line behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Enemy attack handling, AI placement planning, piece generation, and preview state.

## Important Context
- The previous implementation had timed attacks in `frame()` that could add incoming garbage independently of line clears; `enemyClear(n)` already sends garbage only for clears of two or more.
- Recent edits in `game.js` introduced `enemyBag`, `nextEnemyType()`, `enemyPlacement()`, and enemy target-rotation state, but were not yet tested.
- The enemy spawn path now reads `nextTypePreview` or `nextEnemyType()`, then advances the preview. `nextTypePreview` is initialized later as `null`, and `reset()` currently resets `bag` but not `enemyBag`; review this flow.
- Changes are uncommitted. Earlier game checks passed before the latest enemy-AI edits; no validation has been run since those edits.

## Objective
- Expand RuneStack with a human character setup, level-based stats and spell unlocks, and randomized enemies whose AI reflects their species or identity.

## Requirements
- Require creating a named human character before play; show HP, attack, max mana, and percentage-based defense capped at 75%.
- Start at level 1; cap progression at level 100.
- Provide five spell slots, unlocking magic at levels 3, 10, 25, 40, and 70; level 1 starts without spells.
- Randomize encounters; levels 1–10 feature weak enemies or common animals, with stronger enemies appearing later.
- Make enemy AI behavior depend on enemy identity, such as its name, species, or type.

## Decisions
- Use a separate enemy piece bag so the preview matches the enemy’s spawn sequence.
- Score enemy placements using line clears, stack height, holes, and surface unevenness; new work adds species-style weighting.
- Store the player profile and enemy progression in local storage.

### Completed
- Prior checkpoint: timed enemy attacks no longer add garbage; enemy clears of at least two lines can send garbage.
- Prior checkpoint: enemy-specific piece generation, matching next-piece preview, and board-evaluating placement planning were added.
- Added character-creation markup, a character button, and player stat display placeholders in `index.html`.
- Added character-modal styling in `styles.css`.
- Added profile/stat helper functions, level unlock thresholds, and enemy style/tier data in `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish wiring character creation, profile persistence, and the requirement that a character be created before starting play.
- Implement XP/level progression capped at 100, level-scaled HP/attack/mana, defense-based damage reduction, and the five-slot spell loadout with level restrictions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s character progression and combat features, then verify the game’s UI and rules.

## Requirements
- Require a named character before play; show HP, attack, max mana, and defense capped at 75%.
- Start at level 1, cap progression at level 100, and unlock five spell slots at levels 3, 10, 25, 40, and 70.
- Randomize encounters; levels 1–10 feature weak enemies or common animals, with stronger enemies appearing later.
- Make enemy AI behavior depend on its identity, such as name, species, or type.
- Timed enemy attacks damage vitality; only enemy clears of at least two lines send garbage.

## Decisions
- Use a separate enemy piece bag so preview matches enemy spawn sequence.
- Score enemy placements using line clears, stack height, holes, and surface unevenness, weighted by species style.
- Store player profile and enemy progression in local storage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added randomized, tiered enemy encounters, species-derived `HUNTER`, `GUARDIAN`, and `MYSTIC` styles, and persisted enemy advancement.
- Added enemy-specific piece generation with matching preview, board-evaluating placement planning, and style-weighted AI.
- Added character modal markup, player stat display placeholders, modal styling, and profile/stat/unlock helpers.
- Added line-clear XP awards, level-100 cap, attack-scaled line-attack and spell damage, defense-based damage reduction, and UI updates for character stats and equipped spell shortcuts.
- Restricted spell casting to equipped spells and mapped displayed slot shortcuts to equipped spells.
- Validated stored profiles: trimmed names, normalized five spell slots, and rejected spells assigned to locked or mismatched tiers.
- Updated `updateUI()` to show player HP against max HP and call `syncSpellbook()` and `updateProfileUI()`.

### Active
- Wire character creation form submission, validation, cancel behavior, and character-button behavior; initialize profile UI and prevent play before profile creation.
- Fix spell healing to use `state.playerMaxHp`; award XP on victory and refresh unlocked slots after level progression.
- Audit enemy garbage rules, encounter tiers, spell shortcuts, and combat/UI consistency.
- Run `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and browser checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish profile modal event wiring and profile initialization in `game.js`.
2. Fix max-HP healing and award victory XP; verify spell loadout and keyboard slot mapping.
3. Run syntax/diff checks and browser-test profile creation, leveling, encounters, and garbage rules.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, enemy progression, and incomplete character/profile integration.
- `index.html`: Character creation modal and player-stat UI.
- `styles.css`: Character modal and stat styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` had pre-existing uncommitted changes before this work.
- Latest edits have not been syntax-checked or browser-tested.
- Spell healing in `castSpell()` still caps at `100`; `finish(true, ...)` does not yet award victory XP.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s character progression and combat features, then verify the game’s UI and rules.

## Requirements
- Require a named character before play; show HP, attack, max mana, and defense capped at 75%.
- Start at level 1, cap progression at level 100, and unlock five spell slots at levels 3, 10, 25, 40, and 70.
- Randomize encounters; levels 1–10 feature weak enemies or common animals, with stronger enemies appearing later.
- Make enemy AI behavior depend on its identity, such as name, species, or type.
- Timed enemy attacks damage vitality; only enemy clears of at least two lines send garbage.

## Decisions
- Use a separate enemy piece bag so preview matches enemy spawn sequence.
- Score enemy placements using line clears, stack height, holes, and surface unevenness, weighted by species style.
- Store player profile and enemy progression in local storage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented randomized, tiered enemy encounters, species-derived `HUNTER`, `GUARDIAN`, and `MYSTIC` styles, and persisted enemy advancement.
- Added enemy-specific piece generation with matching preview, board-evaluating placement planning, and style-weighted AI.
- Added character modal, stat display, profile/stat/unlock helpers, name validation, cancel behavior, and character-button behavior.
- Validated stored profiles: trimmed names, normalized five spell slots, and rejected spells assigned to locked or mismatched tiers.
- Added line-clear and victory XP, level-100 cap, attack-scaled damage, defense-based damage reduction, and UI updates.
- Restricted spell casting and keyboard shortcuts to equipped spells; capped healing at `state.playerMaxHp`.
- Reset and open character creation when no profile exists; block keyboard controls while the modal is open.
- Browser-tested profile creation and gameplay start; confirmed character editing is blocked during a duel and saw no page errors.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed previously.
- Confirmed `enemyClear()` sends no garbage for one line and sends garbage starting at two lines.

### Active
- Finish browser checks for timed attacks, encounter progression, leveling, and spell loadout/shortcuts.
- Re-run syntax and whitespace checks after any fixes.

### Blocked
- A deeper browser test attempt did not proceed: the character modal correctly intercepted the start-button click before profile creation. `playwright-cli` also expected an unavailable bundled Chromium, though Playwright worked through `/usr/bin/chromium`.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing using Playwright with `/usr/bin/chromium`; create a profile before attempting to start.
2. Verify timed attack damage, level/encounter progression, spell unlocking/equipping, and shortcuts.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, enemy progression, profile integration, and combat.
- `index.html`: Character creation modal and player-stat UI.
- `styles.css`: Character modal and stat styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `game.js` had pre-existing uncommitted changes before this work.
- The latest browser test confirmed profile persistence and gameplay start after character creation; comprehensive rule testing remains pending.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e1901d073ffevmuDlyi1hKYLfR" state="completed">
RuneStack already has working touch controls; no new control implementation is needed.

- **Markup:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:70` defines `.touch-controls` with six buttons: `data-action="left"`, `"rotate"`, `"right"`, `"down"`, `"drop"`, and `"hold"`.
- **Events and actions:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:106` listens for `pointerdown` on `.touch-row button`. Left/right call `move(−1/1)`, rotate calls `rotate()`, drop calls `hardDrop()`, hold calls `holdPiece()`, and down calls `softDrop()` then repeats it every 75 ms. `pointerup`, `pointerleave`, and `pointercancel` clear the repeat interval. The game’s shared movement functions already guard against inactive or paused gameplay.
- **Other gameplay controls:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:105` maps keyboard inputs: arrows or A/D/W/S, X, Space, C/Shift, P/Escape, and number keys 1–5 for equipped spells. Spellbook buttons also cast on `click` (`game.js:37`). The mobile touch controls do **not** include pause; the pause button and keyboard guide are in `.right-panel`, which is hidden on mobile.
- **Responsive state:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css:2` hides `.touch-controls` by default. In the `@media(max-width:700px)` rule on line 5, they become a two-column grid with 42px-high buttons and `touch-action:manipulation`. The same mobile rule stacks `.arena-layout` vertically, orders `.playfield-wrap` before `.player-panel`, and hides `.right-panel`. At widths 701px and above, the touch controls remain hidden.
- **Current placement:** The controls section is after the entire `.arena-layout` in the HTML. On mobile that puts it below the playfield **and** the player panel—not directly beneath the board.

**Minimal recommendation:** If controls should sit immediately under the boards, move the existing `.touch-controls` section into `.playfield-wrap`, just after `.boards-row` and before `.arena-feed`. That keeps the mobile controls in a wide container and avoids shrinking the buttons into the narrower player-board column. Preserve the existing CSS breakpoint and pointer handlers.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s character progression and combat features, and make the game comfortable to play on mobile with controls directly below the Tetris boards.

## Requirements
- Require a named character before play; show HP, attack, max mana, and defense capped at 75%.
- Start at level 1, cap progression at level 100, and unlock five spell slots at levels 3, 10, 25, 40, and 70.
- Randomize encounters; levels 1–10 feature weak enemies or common animals, with stronger enemies appearing later.
- Make enemy AI behavior depend on enemy identity; timed attacks damage vitality; only enemy clears of at least two lines send garbage.
- Support mobile devices and place controls below the player’s board.

## Decisions
- Use a separate enemy piece bag so preview matches enemy spawn sequence.
- Score enemy placements using line clears, stack height, holes, and surface unevenness, weighted by species style.
- Store player profile and enemy progression in local storage.
- Reuse existing touch controls and pointer handlers; place `.touch-controls` inside `.playfield-wrap` immediately after `.boards-row`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-tested character profiles, level/stat progression, spell unlocking/equipping, encounter advancement, enemy attacks, and line-clear garbage rules.
- Moved the existing touch controls beneath `.boards-row` and refined mobile buttons for larger tap targets and touch input.
- Generated a Chromium screenshot at a 390×844 viewport; `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If further verification is needed, test touch interactions in a mobile-sized browser viewport.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Board layout and relocated touch-control markup.
- `styles.css`: Responsive arena and touch-control styling.
- `game.js`: Existing touch pointer handlers and gameplay controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; current modified files are `index.html` and `styles.css`.
- Existing touch actions are handled by pointer events on `.touch-row button`: left/right, rotate, soft drop, hard drop, and hold.
- Mobile screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/runestack-mobile.png`; browser rendering was run, but touch interactions were not exercised in-browser.

messages.text: "Now, enemies can also be affected by \"hold\" (storing a piece for later use). Additionally, whenever the human player levels up, they can manually allocate attribute points—choosing between HP, attack, or defense (starting with 10 points, and gaining 2 to 5 points per level-up). There are now 500 distinct types of enemies; some possess specific spells, while others may have multiple—with high-level enemies potentially wielding up to 5 different spells. The player's game board has been resized to match the dimensions of the enemies' boards. If an enemy with spells appears, their mana bar will also be displayed. Furthermore, each enemy has a unique personality, influencing their playstyle: for instance, some might prioritize clearing lines only when the board is completely tidy, while others might focus on placing pieces along the edges before filling the center to complete lines—leaving a gap of 2 or 3 rows in the middle. Each enemy employs a distinct strategy, though some may share similarities. The difficulty level varies depending on the specific enemy being faced. If the human player is defeated, their XP, level, and name are reset, requiring the creation of a new character. A \"Z\" key has been added, allowing pieces to rotate to the left instead of the right. Finally, some enemies are capable of speaking or making animal sounds—as if some of them were actual animals."

<subagent sessionID="ses_e15d18ce3ffeUN4mrqsqB4ue7b" state="completed">
## Architecture

All game logic is in **`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`**, inside a single IIFE. The main systems share one mutable `state` object; there are no separate AI, spell, or progression modules in this file.

### Enemy AI and enemy list

- **Enemy roster:** `SPECIES`, `EPITHETS`, and `ENEMIES` at lines 23–26. The 400 foes are generated from combinations rather than stored as 400 individual records. Each generated entry includes tier, style, HP, drop and think intervals, attack cadence and damage, magic eligibility, and hard-drop probability.
- **Enemy selection/progression:** `readEnemyIndex()`, `readEnemyStage()`, and `enemyInfo()` at lines 34–36. On victory, `finish()` at line 61 advances the stage and selects a foe from the next tier group, then persists the index and stage.
- **Placement strategy:** `enemyPlacement()` at line 98 tries each rotation and horizontal position, simulates a landing, and scores the resulting board using clears, attack, height, holes, and unevenness—with style-specific adjustments.
- **Movement and timing:** `enemyThink()`, `enemyHardDrop()`, and `updateEnemy()` at lines 99–101 handle the AI’s movement, rotation, probabilistic hard drops, gravity, and spell effects such as stun, slow, and haste. `frame()` at line 102 calls the enemy update and schedules periodic foe attacks.
- **Enemy attacks/board effects:** `enemyClear()`, `consumeGarbage()`, `enemyDamage()`, `enemyGarbage()`, and `burnRows()` at lines 77–81 connect line clears, incoming garbage, and spell damage to combat.

**Likely change points:** roster or difficulty tuning belongs in the constants/generator at lines 23–26; decision quality in `enemyPlacement()`; execution/timing in `enemyThink()` / `updateEnemy()`; attack cadence in `frame()` and the generated enemy fields.

### Pieces and hold

- `SHAPES`, `shuffled()`, `nextType()`, `makePiece()`, and `collides()` define tetrominoes, bag generation, spawning geometry, and collision checks (lines 3–10, 48–51).
- `spawn()` at line 55 refills the player queue and resets the hold allowance. `lockPiece()` at lines 69–73 handles both player and enemy locks, clears, scoring, and respawning.
- `holdPiece()` at line 67 swaps the active piece with the held piece, or advances the queue on the first hold. It enforces one hold per piece via `canHold`.
- `renderPreviews()` at line 96 updates next/hold/enemy previews.

**Likely change points:** hold rules in `holdPiece()` and the `canHold` reset in `spawn()`; queue or piece-generation behavior in the bag helpers and `spawn()`.

### Spells and mana

- `SPELLS` at lines 13–22 defines spell IDs, names, descriptions, mana costs, and icons.
- `playerStats()` at line 29 sets level-derived HP, attack, max mana, and defense. `renderCharacter()` at line 39 builds spell slots/loadout choices; `renderSpellbook()` / `syncSpellbook()` at lines 37–38 show equipped spells and availability.
- `castSpell()` at lines 82–84 checks run state, equipment, mana, and spell-specific preconditions, then deducts mana and applies the effect through its switch.
- Mana is initialized to its maximum in `start()` and `reset()` (lines 59–60), and restored by cleared rows in `lockPiece()` (line 71). Level-ups can raise maximum and current mana in `awardXP()`.

**Likely change points:** adding or retuning spells requires coordinated edits to `SPELLS`, `castSpell()` validation/effect handling, and potentially character-slot tiering (`spellTier()`, `spellsForSlot()`, `LEVEL_UNLOCKS`). Mana earning/capacity changes touch `lockPiece()`, `playerStats()`, `awardXP()`, `start()`, and `reset()`.

### Levels, XP, and death/reset behavior

- Profile persistence and validation: `readProfile()` and `saveProfile()` (lines 27, 33); level stats and unlocks: `playerStats()`, `LEVEL_UNLOCKS`, `spellTier()`, and `spellsForSlot()` (lines 25, 29–32).
- XP thresholds and level-ups: `xpToNext()` and `awardXP()` at lines 42–43. Player line clears award XP in `lockPiece()` (line 71); victories award additional XP in `finish()` (line 61). XP is saved after awards.
- `finish()` marks either victory or defeat and stops the run. On victory it awards XP and advances/persists enemy progression; on defeat it does not reset the profile or enemy progression.
- `reset()` at line 60 clears the run state and restores player stats from the persistent profile. A later `start()` invokes it when restarting after a finished run (line 59). XP already awarded for line clears is persisted even if the run later ends in defeat.

**Likely change points:** XP sources in `lockPiece()` / `finish()`; leveling and stat adjustments in `awardXP()` / `playerStats()`; what persists or clears on death/restart in `finish()` and `reset()`.

### Keyboard controls

`window.addEventListener('keydown', …)` at line 105 handles keyboard input:
- Move: arrows or A/D
- Rotate: up arrow, W, or X
- Soft drop: down arrow or S
- Hard drop: Space
- Hold: C or Shift
- Equipped spells: 1–5
- Pause: P or Escape
- Start: Enter when not running

Touch controls are wired separately at line 106. Spell-button labels and clicks are wired by `renderSpellbook()` at line 37.

**Likely change point:** keyboard mappings and input gating in the keydown handler; keep the touch-control handler in sync if controls change.
</subagent>

<subagent sessionID="ses_e15d18cdcffek1IaWCJoUAK8Ac" state="completed">
## Existing layout and sizing

- **Board:** The player canvas is intrinsically **300 × 600 px** and the opponent canvas **180 × 360 px**; both use a **1:2 aspect ratio**. At the default desktop layout, their CSS widths match those dimensions. [index.html:43–52](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L43) · [game.js:3–4](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L3) · [styles.css:2](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css#L2)
- **Desktop arena:** Three columns: **244 px / flexible center / 244 px**, with 16 px gaps. At widths of at least 1200 px, the side columns grow to **255 px** and the center has a 520 px minimum. [styles.css:2–3](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css#L2)
- **Medium screens (≤1050 px):** The layout becomes a 210 px player panel plus a center column with a 430 px minimum; the right panel is hidden. The boards are set to **250 × 500 px** and **150 × 300 px**. [styles.css:4](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css#L4)
- **Mobile (≤700 px):** The arena stacks vertically, with the player panel below the playfield. The two boards remain side by side and keep the 1:2 ratio; their widths scale with the viewport. The player panel reorganizes into a compact grid, and touch controls are present. [styles.css:5–6](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css#L5) · [index.html:55](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L55)

## Enemy display and status

The opponent header shows **name, foe number/tier, trait, vitality bar, and current status**. The opponent column also includes a board-phase label, next-piece preview, and incoming-attack indicator. The player board has its own phase label and incoming-attack status. [index.html:41–52](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L41)

On mobile, the opponent header and related labels are reduced to very small text sizes (some labels are 7 px). That’s the clearest readability pressure point, especially when identity, health, and status compete for horizontal space. [styles.css:5](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css#L5)

## Player and character progression

The player panel contains identity and level, vitality and XP bars, attack/mana/defense values, score/lines/attack/combo, and the equipped spellbook. The character modal has a name field, four current-stat readouts, and five spell slots with unlock levels **3, 10, 25, 40, and 70**. [index.html:28–37](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L28) · [index.html:72–82](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L72)

Progression is capped at level 100. Wins award `250 + tier × 25` XP; clearing lines also awards XP. Stats scale with level, and the spell slots become available at their stated levels. The creation modal displays stats rather than offering stat allocation. [game.js:25–30](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L25) · [game.js:39–43](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L39) · [game.js:61](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L61) · [game.js:71](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L71)

## Focused UI suggestions

1. **Improve mobile opponent-header legibility.** Give the enemy identity and health/status clearer priority—potentially by wrapping or moving secondary details—rather than shrinking the text further.
2. **Keep key controls available when the right panel is hidden.** That panel contains the pause button, player next/hold previews, keyboard guidance, and combat log. At ≤1050 px the whole panel disappears; consider relocating pause to the playfield header and providing a compact way to access the other information. [index.html:59–68](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L59) · [styles.css:4](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css#L4)
3. **Make progression easier to scan in the character modal.** The unlock levels are stated, but the locked slots show their level individually in muted text. Consider emphasizing the next unlock or visually distinguishing available, equipped, and locked slots.
4. **Preserve board parity while tuning compact layouts.** The existing proportional sizing is consistent; avoid changes that make either board’s cells too small or distort the shared 1:2 ratio.

No files were changed.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand RuneStack’s combat, enemy AI, progression, defeat/reset, keyboard, and dialogue features while preserving the mobile-friendly layout.

## Requirements
- Enemies can hold pieces; add Z for counterclockwise rotation.
- Players start with 10 attribute points and gain 2–5 per level-up to allocate among HP, attack, and defense.
- Generate 500 distinct enemies with varying spell loadouts, up to five spells for high-level enemies; show enemy mana when applicable.
- Match player and enemy board dimensions.
- Defeat resets the player’s name, level, and XP, requiring character creation again.
- Give enemies distinct personalities, strategies, and difficulty; some speak or make animal sounds.

## Decisions
- Enemy roster remains procedurally generated from species/epithet combinations, with added per-enemy strategy, personality, spells, and voice data.
- Both boards use 10 × 20 grids; player canvas is now set to match the enemy canvas’s intrinsic dimensions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Started roster expansion to 500 generated enemies, adding spell-loadout, strategy, personality, voice, difficulty, and hold-chance fields in `game.js`.
- Added enemy mana markup in `index.html` and set the enemy canvas to 300 × 600.
- Added attribute allocation modal markup and styling.
- Added profile attribute/point persistence parsing, attribute-adjusted stats, and initial allocation logic in `game.js`.

### Active
- Complete enemy hold behavior, strategy-specific AI and spell/mana use, and enemy dialogue/animal sounds.
- Finish attribute allocation lifecycle, including modal close/resume behavior and ensuring level-ups do not interrupt gameplay incorrectly.
- Implement Z counterclockwise rotation and update control hints.
- Implement defeat reset and require creation of a new character.
- Update board CSS sizing to preserve parity across desktop, medium, and mobile layouts.
- Validate enemy uniqueness/count, spell scaling, mana UI, and combat interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `game.js` edits and finish allocation, defeat reset, enemy hold/spells, AI strategy, dialogue, and Z rotation.
2. Update `index.html`/`styles.css` sizing and keyboard hints; verify player/enemy boards match at responsive breakpoints.
3. Run syntax and diff checks, then test gameplay and mobile layout.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Enemy roster/AI, player progression, combat, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Board dimensions, enemy status/mana UI, controls, and character/allocation modals.
- `styles.css`: Responsive board sizing and modal/status styling.

## Important Context
- `game.js` is a single IIFE with a shared mutable `state`.
- Existing AI uses `enemyPlacement()`, `enemyThink()`, and `updateEnemy()`; player hold is implemented by `holdPiece()`.
- Existing enemy list had 400 generated entries; `readEnemyIndex()` still clamps saved selection to 399 and UI text still references `/ 400`.
- Current allocation code pauses on level-up and opens `#attributeModal`, but modal allocation handlers/close flow and pausing integration remain to be implemented.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8:

21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.

## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s combat, enemy AI, progression, defeat/reset, keyboard, and dialogue features while preserving mobile-friendly layout.

## Requirements
- Enemies can hold pieces; add Z for counterclockwise rotation.
- Start players with 10 attribute points; award 2–5 points per level-up for HP, attack, and defense.
- Generate 500 distinct enemies with varied spell loadouts (up to five spells for high-level enemies) and display enemy mana when applicable.
- Match player and enemy board dimensions.
- Defeat resets the player’s name, level, and XP, requiring character creation again.
- Give enemies distinct personalities, strategies, difficulty; some speak or make animal sounds.

## Decisions
- Generate the enemy roster from species/epithet combinations, with per-enemy strategy, personality, spells, voice, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Both boards use 10 × 20 grids and 300 × 600 intrinsic canvas dimensions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Generated 500 enemy entries with varied metadata and spell loadouts in `game.js`; added enemy mana markup and 300 × 600 enemy canvas in `index.html`.
- Added profile parsing, attribute-adjusted stats, initial allocation and level-up point award logic.
- Wired new-character submission to save attributes and 10 initial points, open the allocation modal, and preserve profile fields; added allocation and done handlers with gameplay pause/resume support.
- Added enemy mana initialization and UI synchronization; added strategy-specific placement scoring and enemy piece-hold logic.
- Added preliminary enemy spell-casting effects and enemy shield/mirror handling.
- Added defeat logic that clears the saved profile and reopens character creation.
- Changes remain uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`.

### Active
- Wire and validate enemy spell casting in the game loop, mana regeneration, and enemy dialogue during combat.
- Wire Z to `rotateCCW()`, fix remaining `/ 400` text in `reset()`, and verify responsive board dimensions.
- Verify initial and level-up allocation lifecycle, defeat reset to level 1/0 XP, enemy roster uniqueness/count and spell scaling, combat, and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- None

## Next Move
1. Connect enemy casting and mana regeneration to the game loop; update mana display and add occasional personality dialogue.
2. Wire Z rotation, fix the roster count text in `reset()`, and check responsive sizing for both boards.
3. Run syntax and gameplay/layout checks; inspect and correct allocation, defeat-reset, and combat edge cases.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Roster generation, progression, allocation, combat, enemy AI, input, and rendering.

## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s combat, enemy AI, progression, defeat/reset, keyboard, and dialogue features while preserving a mobile-friendly layout.

## Requirements
- Enemies can hold pieces; add Z for counterclockwise rotation.
- Start players with 10 attribute points; award 2–5 points per level-up for HP, attack, and defense.
- Generate 500 distinct enemies with varied spell loadouts (up to five spells for high-level enemies) and display enemy mana when applicable.
- Match player and enemy board dimensions.
- Defeat resets the player’s name, level, and XP, requiring character creation again.
- Give enemies distinct personalities, strategies, difficulty; some speak or make animal sounds.

## Decisions
- Generate the enemy roster from species/epithet combinations, with per-enemy strategy, personality, spells, voice, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Both boards use 10 × 20 grids and 300 × 600 intrinsic canvas dimensions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Generated 500 enemy entries with varied metadata and spell loadouts; added enemy mana markup and 300 × 600 enemy canvas.
- Added profile parsing, attribute-adjusted stats, initial allocation and level-up point award logic.
- Wired new-character submission to save profile attributes and 10 initial points, open allocation, and preserve profile fields; added allocation and done handlers with gameplay pause/resume support.
- Added enemy mana initialization and UI synchronization; added strategy-specific placement scoring and enemy piece-hold logic.
- Added preliminary enemy spell-casting effects, enemy shield/mirror handling, and player hex behavior.
- Added defeat logic that clears the saved profile and reopens character creation.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest edits; changes remain uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`.

### Active
- Connect enemy casting and mana regeneration to the game loop; add occasional personality dialogue during combat.
- Wire Z to `rotateCCW()`, fix remaining `/ 400` text in `reset()`, and verify responsive board dimensions.
- Verify initial and level-up allocation lifecycle, defeat reset to level 1/0 XP, enemy roster uniqueness/count and spell scaling, combat, and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- None

## Next Move
1. Wire enemy spell casting and mana regeneration into the game loop, update mana display, and add enemy dialogue.
2. Wire Z rotation, update the roster count in `reset()`, and check responsive sizing for both boards.
3. Run syntax and gameplay/layout checks; inspect and correct allocation, defeat-reset, and combat edge cases.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Roster generation, progression, allocation, combat, enemy AI, input, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Boards, enemy status/mana UI, controls, and character/allocation modals.
- `styles.css`: Responsive board sizing and modal/status styling.

## Important Context
- `rotateCCW(m)` exists but Z is not yet wired.
- `enemyCastSpell()` and `enemyBurnRows()` are implemented, but game-loop casting and mana regeneration remain unwired.
- Enemy mana UI syncs through `updateUI()`; enemy dialogue during combat is still missing.
- `reset()` still shows `FOE … / 400`; enemy roster contains 500 entries.
- Latest `node --check game.js` and `git status --short` completed; syntax check passed and the three listed files are modified.

## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s combat, enemy AI, progression, defeat/reset, keyboard, and dialogue features while preserving a mobile-friendly layout.

## Requirements
- Enemies can hold pieces; add Z for counterclockwise rotation.
- Start players with 10 attribute points; award 2–5 points per level-up for HP, attack, and defense.
- Generate 500 distinct enemies with varied spell loadouts (up to five spells for high-level enemies) and display enemy mana when applicable.
- Match player and enemy board dimensions.
- Defeat resets the player’s name, level, and XP, requiring character creation again.
- Give enemies distinct personalities, strategies, difficulty; some speak or make animal sounds.

## Decisions
- Generate the enemy roster from species/epithet combinations, with per-enemy strategy, personality, spells, voice, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Both boards use 10 × 20 grids and 300 × 600 intrinsic canvas dimensions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented 500 generated enemy entries, enemy mana UI, and matching enemy canvas.
- Added profile parsing, attribute-adjusted stats, starting allocation and level-up point awards.
- Added enemy spell casting, mana regeneration, strategy-based placement, hold behavior, and occasional personality or animal-voice dialogue.
- Added defeat profile clearing and character creation reopening.
- Added player stun and silence effects; enemies stop casting while player silence is active.
- Updated `reset()` to clear player/enemy combat, spell, hold, and timing state, using the current enemy and player stats.
- Added `rotateCounterclockwise()` with collision checks and wall kicks.

### Active
- Wire the Z-key handler to call `rotateCounterclockwise()`; it currently calls `rotateCCW()`, the matrix-only helper.
- Verify allocation pause/resume and defeat-to-new-character flow; exercise combat effects and AI.
- Test responsive layout on desktop and mobile, then run syntax and whitespace checks.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification remains pending; prior checkpoint identified a likely syntax error in `reset()`, but its duplicate `foe` declaration was addressed in the latest edit. Syntax has not yet been checked.

## Next Move
1. Change the Z-key handler to call `rotateCounterclockwise()`.
2. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
3. Verify gameplay flows, combat effects, AI, and desktop/mobile responsive layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Enemy roster, progression, allocation, combat, AI, input, and reset logic.
- `index.html`: Game boards, enemy mana/status UI, controls, and character/allocation modals.
- `styles.css`: Responsive board sizing, status styling, and modals.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s combat, enemy AI, progression, defeat/reset, keyboard, and dialogue features while preserving a mobile-friendly layout.

## Requirements
- Enemies can hold pieces; add Z for counterclockwise rotation.
- Start players with 10 attribute points; award 2–5 points per level-up for HP, attack, and defense.
- Generate 500 distinct enemies with varied spell loadouts (up to five spells for high-level enemies) and display enemy mana when applicable.
- Match player and enemy board dimensions.
- Defeat resets the player’s name, level, and XP, requiring character creation again.
- Give enemies distinct personalities, strategies, difficulty; some speak or make animal sounds.

## Decisions
- Generate the enemy roster from species/epithet combinations, with per-enemy strategy, personality, spells, voice, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Both boards use 10 × 20 grids and 300 × 600 intrinsic canvas dimensions.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented 500 generated enemies, enemy mana UI, and matching enemy canvas.
- Added profile parsing, attribute-adjusted stats, starting allocation and level-up point awards.
- Added enemy spell casting, mana regeneration, strategy-based placement, hold behavior, and occasional personality or animal-voice dialogue.
- Added defeat profile clearing and character creation reopening.
- Added player stun and silence effects; enemies stop casting while player silence is active.
- Updated `reset()` to clear player/enemy combat, spell, hold, and timing state.
- Added collision-checked counterclockwise rotation; Z-key handler calls `rotateCounterclockwise()`.
- Browser-tested new character creation, allocation of all 10 starting points, matching board canvas sizes, pause/resume, responsive layout at desktop and mobile widths, and defeat reopening character creation with `runestack-player` cleared.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Review any further gameplay/layout issues if requested.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Report the implemented changes and browser verification results; no pending implementation step is identified.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Enemy roster, progression, allocation, combat, AI, input, and reset logic.
- `index.html`: Game boards, enemy mana/status UI, controls, and character/allocation modals.
- `styles.css`: Responsive board sizing, status styling, and modals.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.
- Local HTTP server was available at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`; Chromium gameplay checks confirmed defeat displays `DEFEAT`, opens character creation, and removes `runestack-player` from local storage.

Damage can also be dealt via spells if an enemy uses one against the player. (This effectively fixes an issue where the player would take damage automatically, even when the enemy hadn't completed 2 lines or used a spell.) Each specific enemy has its own attack stat, defense percentage, and total HP. The total number of enemies has been set to 900. If an enemy possesses mana, the specific spell(s) they can cast will be displayed; enemy mana does not regenerate automatically, though they begin each encounter with a full mana bar. The player’s mana—tracked separately from the enemies—is fully restored at the start of every new battle or encounter. Additionally, the player's defense stat has been increased by 0.20% to improve game balance, and the player's base attack has been adjusted from 8 to 5. Finally, the player's HP is now fully restored whenever they win a fight or begin a new one.

## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s combat balance and 900-enemy roster updates, then verify gameplay and responsive layouts.

## Requirements
- Generate 900 distinct enemies with individual attack, defense, HP, and spell loadouts; display possessed spells and mana UI.
- Enemy mana starts full each encounter and does not regenerate; restore player HP and mana at battle start, and restore HP after victory.
- Player damage occurs only when an enemy clears at least 2 lines or casts a damaging spell; line-clear damage scales with lines cleared.

- Keep both boards at 10 × 20 with 300 × 600 canvases; defeat clears profile data and returns to character creation.

## Decisions
- Generate enemies from species/epithet combinations with varied personalities, strategies, spells, voices, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Retain line-clear and spell damage paths; remove automatic timed enemy damage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded enemy generation to 900 and added per-enemy attack and defense fields.
- Set player base attack to 5; set enemy mana to full at battle start and removed mana regeneration.
- Removed timed automatic enemy damage and scaled enemy line-clear damage by lines cleared, starting at 2 lines.

- Updated the visible roster count to 900.

1. Remove the extra brace in `playerStats()` and run `node --check game.js`.
2. Review enemy attack/defense fields and defense scaling to ensure they affect combat as intended.
3. Run browser verification for roster, combat damage, mana, restoration, defeat reset, controls, and responsive layouts.

- `game.js`: Enemy generator, stats, combat/damage, mana, spells, and battle lifecycle.

## Objective
- Complete RuneStack’s combat balance and enemy roster updates, then verify gameplay and responsive layouts.
- Finish mana allocation, enemy attribute/HP display, Champion tier label, and progression through the 900-enemy roster.

## Requirements
- Create 900 enemies across tiers 1–11 with counts `100, 150, 150, 100, 100, 100, 50, 50, 25, 25, 50`; Tier 11 is “Champion.”
- Player defense scaling increases by 0.2%; maximum mana can be upgraded to 50.
- Show every enemy attribute and display enemy HP as current/maximum absolute values, not a percentage.
- Halve basic enemy level unlock thresholds (for example, level 10 becomes level 5).
- Preserve prior combat, roster, restoration, and responsive-layout requirements.

## Decisions
- Generate enemies from species/epithet combinations, preserving varied personalities, strategies, spells, voices, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Retain line-clear and spell damage; remove automatic timed enemy damage.
- Use tier-based spell scaling that progresses across the 11 tiers.
- Use cumulative tier counts for roster progression rather than assuming 10 enemies per tier.

## Work State
### Completed
- Generated the 900-enemy roster using `TIER_COUNTS=[100,150,150,100,100,100,50,50,25,25,50]`.
- Set level unlocks to `[3,5,13,20,35]`.
- Added mana to normalized saved attributes; `playerStats()` includes upgrades, caps mana at 50, and computes defense scaling.
- Existing code includes allocation controls for HP, attack, and defense, plus enemy vitality/mana UI.

### Active
- Add mana to attribute allocation UI and implement allocation with a 50-point maximum.
- Display every enemy attribute and absolute current/maximum HP.
- Label Tier 11 “Champion”; update rank display and victory progression to navigate the 11-tier roster correctly.
- Verify combat and responsive layouts.

### Blocked
- Interactive browser automation was previously unavailable because `playwright` was not found.

## Next Move
1. Add mana as an attribute choice, show its allocated count, and prevent upgrades above the 50 mana cap.
2. Add enemy attribute display and current/maximum HP; ensure foe rank uses Champion for Tier 11.
3. Replace 10-enemy-tier logic in `finish()` progression with cumulative tier boundaries.
4. Run syntax checks and available gameplay/layout verification.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Roster generation, progression, attributes, combat, and UI updates.
- `index.html`: Player and enemy stat display markup and attribute allocation controls.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layouts and stat panel styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/runestack-final-desktop.png`: Earlier desktop screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/runestack-final-mobile.png`: Earlier mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- `game.js` and `index.html` have uncommitted changes; `styles.css` is also part of the responsive UI work.
- `renderAttributeAllocation()` and `allocateAttribute()` currently support only `hp`, `attack`, and `defense`.
- `updateUI()` currently displays enemy HP as a percentage; `reset()` sets rank to `FOE … · TIER ${foe.tier}`.
- `finish()` still selects tiers using `Math.floor(state.enemyStage/10)+1` and 10-enemy offsets.

## Objective
- Continue RuneStack’s combat-balance and roster work, incorporating the user’s newer requests for enemy archetypes and smarter AI, revised leveling/XP behavior, and player/enemy hold mechanics.

## Requirements
- Maintain 900 enemies across Tiers 1–11, with tier counts `100, 150, 150, 100, 100, 100, 50, 50, 25, 25, 50`; Tier 11 is “Champion.”
- Enemy attributes should vary by role, including high-attack enemies, high-HP tanks, and enemies with defense exceeding attack; most enemies should remain easy, with some very difficult enemies at any tier.
- Leveling should grant only the existing small HP increase; defense should increase only through allocated defense points.
- Give enemies stronger board-state awareness and more strategic piece placement; enemies may share or have unique playstyles, and difficulty can come from speed and strategy.
- Add a player hold mechanic and retain enemy hold behavior; many lower-tier enemies may never hold.
- Award 25% XP when the player completes a full line; accumulate sufficient XP but apply level-ups only after defeating an enemy.
- Preserve earlier combat, roster, restoration, and responsive-layout requirements: defense allocation scaling, mana allocation up to 50, enemy attributes and absolute HP display, halved basic enemy unlock thresholds, and cumulative tier progression.

## Decisions
- Enemies are generated from species/epithet combinations, preserving varied personalities, strategies, spells, voices, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Retain line-clear and spell damage; remove automatic timed enemy damage.
- Use tier-based spell scaling across the 11 tiers.
- Use cumulative tier counts rather than assuming 10 enemies per tier.
- Browser automation was unavailable earlier because `playwright` could not be found.

### Active

- Adjust leveling so level-ups increase HP only, while defense increases only through allocated points.
- Implement XP accrual/bonus for a full line and defer applying level-ups until an enemy is defeated.
- Add player hold controls and tune enemy hold usage, especially disabling it for many low-tier enemies.
- Verify balance, gameplay, and responsive layouts.

### Blocked
- Interactive browser automation was previously unavailable because `playwright` was not found.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` to understand progression, XP, enemy AI, and input handling before modifying.
2. Implement role-based enemy stats/playstyles and board-aware AI, ensuring most opponents remain easy while including strategically challenging outliers.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue RuneStack’s combat-balance and roster work, including enemy archetypes and smarter AI, revised leveling/XP behavior, and player/enemy hold mechanics.

## Requirements
- Maintain 900 enemies across Tiers 1–11 with counts `100, 150, 150, 100, 100, 100, 50, 50, 25, 25, 50`; Tier 11 is “Champion.”
- Vary enemy attributes by role: high-attack enemies, high-HP tanks, and enemies whose defense exceeds attack; most should be easy, with very difficult opponents possible at any tier.
- Leveling should grant only the existing small HP increase; defense should increase only through allocated defense points.
- Improve board-aware enemy placement and strategy; enemies may share or have unique playstyles, and difficulty can come from speed and strategy.
- Support player and enemy hold mechanics; many lower-tier enemies may never hold.
- Award 25% XP when the player completes a full line; retain accumulated XP but apply level-ups only after defeating an enemy.
- Preserve earlier combat, roster, restoration, and responsive-layout requirements: defense allocation scaling, mana allocation up to 50, enemy attributes and absolute HP display, halved basic enemy unlock thresholds, and cumulative tier progression.

## Decisions
- Enemies are generated from species/epithet combinations, preserving varied personalities, strategies, spells, voices, difficulty, and hold chance.
- Retain line-clear and spell damage; remove automatic timed enemy damage.
- Use tier-based spell scaling across the 11 tiers.
- Use cumulative tier counts rather than assuming 10 enemies per tier.

## Work State
### Completed
- Generated the 900-enemy roster with required tier counts and unlock levels `[3,5,13,20,35]`.
- Added mana to saved attributes; `playerStats()` caps mana at 50 and computes defense scaling.
- Added mana allocation controls and cap checks; mana allocation updates in-combat mana.
- Added enemy attribute and absolute HP markup; `updateUI()` fills enemy attributes and HP values and updates enemy name/rank/trait with progression.
- Tier 11 rank labeling displays “CHAMPION.”
- Character creation initializes mana attributes; progression guards against advancing past the final roster tier.
- Player hold already exists (`holdPiece()`, `C`/`Shift`, and touch HOLD control); enemy hold logic and tier-based hold chance already exist.
- Added an `ARCHETYPES` constant to `game.js` defining `RAVAGER`, `TANK`, `BULWARK`, and `TACTICIAN`.

### Active
- Apply archetype-based enemy stats and distribute easy opponents and challenging outliers across all tiers.
- Improve enemy board-state scoring and strategic placement.
- Remove level-derived defense from `playerStats()` while retaining defense-point scaling.
- Change XP accrual to the requested 25% full-line award and defer processing level-ups until enemy victory.
- Tune enemy hold behavior, including disabling it for many low-tier opponents.
- Verify balance, gameplay, and responsive layouts.

### Blocked
- Browser automation was previously unavailable because `playwright` could not be found.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` around enemy generation and apply archetype-scaled stats; the attempted replacement failed because the exact source text did not match.
2. Update enemy AI scoring and speed/difficulty distribution while preserving easy opponents and low-tier no-hold cases.
3. Revise defense scaling and XP accrual/level-up timing.
4. Run syntax checks and available gameplay/responsive checks; report verification limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Enemy generation, player stats, XP/level progression, combat, AI, controls, and UI updates.
- `index.html`: Game UI, enemy stats display, character progression controls, and control markup.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layouts and styling.

## Important Context
- Current `playerStats()` still includes level-derived defense: `((Math.floor(level*.75)+attrs.defense*2)*.002)*100`.
- Current `awardXP()` applies level-ups immediately; line clears currently call `awardXP(cleared*35)`.
- `finish()` awards victory XP and advances enemies using cumulative tier counts.
- Enemy AI uses `enemyPlacement()` scoring and `enemyThink()` for movement, rotation, and probabilistic hold.
- The attempted enemy-generation edit failed with “Could not find oldString in game.js”; only the `ARCHETYPES` constant was successfully added in this latest work.
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js` and `index.html`; `styles.css` was unchanged in the latest status check.

content.text:
Let me understand the request. The user says:

"Now can you make a, the human player receives an amount of XP upon completing lines during the battle (the amount of XP received upon completing a line is 5%), if the player defeats an enemy, they receive an additional 150% of the XP value, with the amount of xp depending on whether the enemy is stronger or weaker."

So:
- Line clear XP: 5% of XP to next level (currently 25%).
- Defeating enemy: additional 150% of the XP value (of what? XP value presumably the line-clear XP amount, or xpToNext). "with the amount of xp depending on whether the enemy is stronger or weaker" — scale the XP grant based on enemy strength relative to player (tier/difficulty).

Currently line clear awards `Math.ceil(xpToNext(profile?.level||1)*.25)*cleared`. Victory awards `awardXP(250+enemyInfo().tier*25)`.

Need to decide a design: line-clearing = 5% of XP to next level per line. Enemy kill = 150% of some XP value, scaled by relative enemy strength. Probably base kill XP = xpToNext * 1.5, multiplied by strength factor based on enemy tier/level vs player level. "with the amount of xp depending on whether the enemy is stronger or weaker" — a multiplier.

Let me look at the codebase to determine level/tier mapping and xpToNext. Let me read the relevant regions.

Let me check game.js top for xpToNext, TIER_COUNTS, LEVEL_UNLOCKS, enemyInfo, etc.

I should ask clarifying question? The requirement is somewhat ambiguous but I can implement reasonably. Existing behavior maybe I should just implement. The instruction says implement. Let me inspect.

Plan:
1. Add `enemyXpMultiplier()` based on enemy tier vs player "expected tier" at level. Or use enemy attack/hp vs player. Simplest: strength ratio based on tier relative to player's level-derived tier.

Mapping: TIER_COUNTS with 11 tiers, unlock levels [3,5,13,20,35] for spells. Character max level 100. Enemy tier 1-11. A reasonable comparison: expected tier = clamp(ceil(profile.level / 10), 1, 11)? That means level 1-10 → tier 1, level 100 → tier 10; hmm 11 tiers. Maybe expected tier = Math.min(11, Math.ceil(level/10)) gives tier 11 at level 100? ceil(100/10)=10. Use ceil(level/9.09)... Let's do `Math.min(11, 1 + Math.floor(level / 10))` → level 1-9 tier 1, 10-19 tier 2, ... 100 → 11. Good.

Kill XP: base = xpToNext(level) * 1.5 (150% of XP value). Strength multiplier: compare enemy tier to expected tier: `mult = clamp(1 + (enemy.tier - expectedTier) * 0.15, 0.5, 2)`. Stronger enemies give more, weaker less. Also hard enemies bonus? Could factor `foe.hard ? 1.1 : 1`. Keep it modest.

Line clear: 5% of xpToNext per line: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(xpToNext(level)*0.05)) * cleared`. Previously 25%. Should I use per-line? Yes "amount of XP received upon completing a line is 5%".

Also note `awardXP` caps at level 100 and returns if level >= 100. Fine.

Also note victory currently `awardXP(250+enemyInfo().tier*25)`. Replace.

Also the checkpoint says "Award 25% XP per full line; retain XP but process level-ups only after enemy victory." New requirement changes 25% → 5%. Also kill bonus 150%.

- Level 1 vs. even Tier 1: 30 XP/line, **900 XP** victory.

We need to design a difficulty audit across all 900 enemies and expose adjustability of behavior. Options:

1. Add a difficulty score computation function `enemyDifficulty(foe)` that quantifies:
   - Speed: dropMs, thinkMs, hardDrop chance (faster = harder)
   - Skill/placement quality: thinkMs (more thinking = better moves), strategy quality weighting, style/archetype.
   - Durability: hp, defense
   - Damage: attack, attackDamage, spells count, magic, enemyManaMax
   - Hold chance.
   - Tier.
   Then produce a rating 1-100 / labels (Easy, Normal, Hard, Elite, Champion) and perhaps compare to expected difficulty by tier to detect outliers (too hard/too easy for its tier).

2. Add a "difficulty audit" mode/tool: a dev/debug UI? The user says "poder ajustar tipo de comportamento deles. ou do jeito que eles meio que joga" — be able to adjust their behavior type/way of playing. This suggests exposing difficulty profile / behavior archetype per enemy and tuning. Could implement:
   - `enemyBehaviorProfile` derived from stats (RUSHER, TACTICIAN, BRUISER, BALANCED, ERRATIC, etc.) and make behavior consistent with archetype/strategy.
   - A tuning layer: `ENEMY_TUNING` object with per-archetype/strategy multipliers for speed, AI quality (planning skill), aggression, hold usage, etc. Then apply during generation or at runtime.
   - "check each difficulty" — an audit function that loops all 900 and reports distribution/outliers; perhaps output to console, or a script `tools/audit-enemies.js`. Since game.js is an IIFE with DOM access, a separate script could duplicate generation—not ideal. Better to expose a function on `window.RuneStack` for audit? Or add a dev panel UI.

We need to infer the best deliverable. The user likely wants the game itself to have varied, sensible difficulty per enemy and the ability to adjust behavior. They ask "consegue ajustar e checar a dificuldade de cada inimigo especifica... sendo total dos 900 ... checar todos eles e checar a cada dificuldade deles. e poder ajustar tipo de comportamento deles."

A. Add a behavior/difficulty system in game.js:
   - Define behavior profiles keyed by strategy/archetype maybe `ENEMY_STYLES` with configuration:
     ```
     const BEHAVIORS={
       RUSHER:{label:'RUSHER', speed:1.18, quality:.35, hold:.6, aggression:1.2},
       ...
     }
     ```
     But enemies already have `strategy`, `archetype`, `style`. We can derive behavior from strategy. "tipo de comportamento deles" could simply be the existing strategy, but make it explicit and tunable.
   - Add `enemyDifficulty(foe)` returns score and details.
   - Add `enemyDifficultyBand(score)` label.
